title: FinePrint knowledge bundle (bundle.json)
description: Contract between the pipeline (producer) and the app (consumer). Bump schema_version on any breaking change. v1.1 (additive): companies, data_flows, device_reach, status sub-types, source independence and archives, Exodus report pinning, stale flag, a required verbatim quote on every source (with as_of, or accessed for undated pages, and verify_url for pages that block scripts), sourced procedural notes on legal items, and risk-tag qualifiers. v1.2 (additive): company short names; health, financial, biometric and children's data kinds for the tier rules; flow ids and in-app controls for the 'What you can do' checklist (a limit can be marked inferred, with a note); sourced summary notes. v1.3: covers (one tracker explanation for several tracker ids) and in_owner_apps (how a tracker's flow reads inside its owner's own apps); in_force and closed_date on legal items, so only ongoing or recent ones count toward a tier; changes[] on app records, each with a direction build.py derives from the record's structure; government lines (recipient_kind government_body: can_compel, has_bought, has_used), a required jurisdiction on companies with its sources, and jurisdictions.json, the laws by which each country can compel data (its own file, defined under $defs/jurisdictions_file); policy_region on app records, and default (on, off, opt_in) on flows. Tracker names and signatures live in trackers.json (ODbL); this file references trackers by id only and never copies Exodus fields.

device_reach.description: Plain-language boilerplate for capabilities an app registers beyond permissions, detected from its manifest at scan time.

status.description: How strong the claim is. Wording in the UI follows this.

status_kind.description: Sub-type of the status. adjudicated: ruling, settlement, settlement_no_admission, regulator_finding, consent_order. alleged: filed, survived_motion_to_dismiss, dismissed.

evidence_tier.description: How a finding was made on-device. Never upgrade contains_code to observed_contact.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. US, CA, IE.

government_line.description: How a government can get the data (docs/METHOD.md, Governments): a law that lets it demand the data, a documented purchase, or documented use reported by at least two sources.

government_detail.description: A line about a government body names its kind of line and its country, and never a company as recipient.

partial_date.description: A full date, or year and month when only the month is known (e.g. a breach dated 'March 2024').

status_detail.description: Status sub-type rules shared by consequences, flows and legal events.

id.description: Needed when another source derives from this one.

as_of.description: The source's own date: publication, filing, ruling or policy version.

accessed.description: When FinePrint read the page. Used instead of as_of when the page carries no date of its own.

quote.description: Required. Verbatim excerpt that supports the claim the source is cited for; fragments may be joined with ' … '. Under 15 words if from a copyrighted source.

derives_from.description: Id of the original source when this one re-reports it, so copies don't count as independent.

single_source.description: The claim rests on one original investigation or study.

vendor_archive_url.description: A dated prior version hosted by the vendor itself (useful, not independent).

verify_url.description: Address build.py fetches instead of url when the page itself blocks scripts: the same article's API (e.g. a help centre's JSON) or an archived copy. url stays the page people read.

procedural_note.description: Where a legal matter stands procedurally (dismissals, appeals), with each part sourced. It never changes the claim's status.

text.description: Plain-language consequence for the user, one or two sentences.

in_force.description: An order or settlement whose terms still bind the company, e.g. a 20-year FTC order. Like appeal_pending, it makes the matter ongoing.

closed_date.description: When the matter ended: a final judgment, a settlement's final approval, an order's expiry. An ongoing matter has none. Ongoing matters, and those dated (closed_date, else date) within three years, count toward a tier.

wording.description: Attribution phrase the UI shows, e.g. 'alleged in a lawsuit filed by the Texas AG on 2025-01-13 (not proven in court)'.

historical.description: True when this describes a past practice, not a current one.

subject_company.description: Who the action is against, when that is not the app's developer.

recipient_kind.description: government_body for a line about a government: shown with the country's laws, never counted toward a tier.

jurisdiction.description: The government's country, for a government_body line.

concerns_app.description: Package whose data the action concerns.

sources.description: The first source is the primary one.

data_flow.description: One line of the explanation screen: what data goes where, for what, and how far.

id.description: Lets the app's controls name the flows they limit.

recipient_label.description: Used when the recipient is unnamed, e.g. 'select business partners', or is a government body, e.g. 'US Department of Homeland Security'.

recipient_kind.description: Left out for a company. A government_body line shows with its country's laws (Jurisdictions), never under the three buckets, and never counts toward a tier.

jurisdiction.description: The government's country, for a government_body line.

bucket.description: stays_here: runs or improves the app. used_for_more: same company, beyond the app (ads, profiling, other products). goes_elsewhere: shared, licensed or sold to other companies.

default.description: Whether the flow happens unless you act: on (the default when left out), off (only if you turn a setting on), opt_in (only if you agree when the app asks). An off flow that a control in the record limits doesn't count toward the tier.

in_owner_apps.description: Tracker records only: the bucket this flow takes when the tracker is in an app made by the tracker's owner company, where nothing goes elsewhere. Left out, a goes_elsewhere flow isn't shown in those apps; the app's own record says what its maker does.

sources.description: The first source is the primary one.

in_force.description: An order or settlement whose terms still bind the company, e.g. a 20-year FTC order. Like appeal_pending, it makes the matter ongoing.

closed_date.description: When the matter ended: a final judgment, a settlement's final approval, an order's expiry. An ongoing matter has none. Ongoing matters, and those dated (closed_date, else date) within three years, count toward a tier.

sources.description: The first source is the primary one.

short_name.description: Name for running text, e.g. 'Allstate' for The Allstate Corporation. Defaults to name.

jurisdiction.description: The country whose law the company is organized under (where it is registered): so it is subject to that country's law.

headquarters.description: The country of its head office, when a source says so. A separate claim from jurisdiction, and from where its servers are, which records never assert.

jurisdiction_sources.description: Corporate registration sources for jurisdiction and headquarters: filings, registries, government orders.

tracker.description: FinePrint's explanation of a tracker. Name, signatures and Exodus categories come from trackers.json.

id.description: Exodus tracker ID where one exists; fp-* for trackers we add ourselves, and for a record that covers several ids.

covers.description: Tracker ids in trackers.json that this one explanation applies to, e.g. Meta's kits (exodus-47, exodus-65, ...). Each id has one explanation at most. With covers, the record's own id need not be in trackers.json.

name.description: Only for fp-* trackers; Exodus names stay in trackers.json.

party.description: first_party when the tracker owner also makes the apps it is usually found in.

product_line.description: Which product this record covers, e.g. 'Kochava attribution' vs 'Kochava Collective'.

monetization_model.description: What the owner does with the data, plainly.

package_id.description: Android package name. iOS bundle IDs go in ios_bundle_id.

summary.description: One paragraph. Opens with what the app does for the user and what it needs for that (copy rules: docs/METHOD.md).

risk_tags.description: Each tag must be backed by a flow or consequence in the record.

risk_tag_notes.description: Qualifier the UI shows with a tag, e.g. regulatory_action: "against Allstate/Arity concerning this app's data". build.py requires one for regulatory_action when no action in the record is against the app's own developer.

trackers.description: Tracker IDs expected in this app, per Exodus or our own analysis. The app shows what it actually detected; this is the reference.

summary_notes.description: Short sourced lines shown under the summary, such as what the app's policy says it doesn't do.

controls.description: In-app settings that limit this app's flows: the user-ticked half of the 'What you can do' checklist. Android permission items are worked out on the device.

changes.description: The record's history: what changed and when. Each direction is derived by build.py from a structural diff against the previous record, never typed.

policy_region.description: The region whose version of the app's privacy policy the record follows, when the app publishes one per region (TikTok: US). The app says so under the summary.

privacy_controls.description: Where in the app the user can switch sharing off (text only).

coverage.description: curated = human-reviewed record; auto = generated from tracker records only, no app-specific claims.

stale.description: Computed by build.py: last_reviewed more than 180 days before the build.

change.description: One change to an app's record. The reviewer writes date, text and sources; build.py --previous adds diff and direction.

direction.description: Derived from diff (docs/METHOD.md, 'Changes to a record'): worsened if any item is a worsening, else improved if any is an improvement, else neutral (wording only).

items.pattern: ^(flow added|flow removed|moved toward stays here|moved away from stays here|data kind added|data kind removed|tracker added|tracker removed|control added|control removed|now off by default|now on by default):

diff.description: The structural changes build.py found between the previous record and this one; empty for a wording-only change.

tier_before.description: The tier before the change, when the reviewer records it.

control.description: An in-app setting the user can change, and the flows (by id, in the same app record) it limits.

label.description: The setting's name as the app shows it, e.g. 'Your Privacy Choices'.

how.description: Where to find it, e.g. 'In the Life360 app: Settings > Privacy > Your Privacy Choices'.

effect.description: What turning it off changes, in the app's own quoted words (attributed), or e.g. "Life360 doesn't say what changes."

anyOf.description: A flow the control limits, marked inferred when the sources don't say so in as many words; an inferred entry needs a note saying what is inferred.

jurisdictions_file.description: bundle/jurisdictions.json (CC BY 4.0), written by build.py from pipeline/reviewed: for each country, the laws that let its government compel a company to hand over data. Every entry is reviewed by the owner; a law is quoted from its own text (status self_disclosed).

name.description: The country's name as the app shows it, the same form for every country.

law.description: A law in force that lets the country's government compel a company to provide data (a Can compel line).

text.description: What it lets the government do, in neutral plain words.

status.description: Quoted from the law's own text.

status_note.description: Where the law stands (a renewal, a sunset), with sources.

sources.description: The first is the law's official text (type statute).

plain.description: What this lets the app do, in one sentence.

why_it_matters.description: What this permission plus a tracker can turn into.

feeds.description: Which data_flow data kinds this permission gives access to.
